svg.title: Update both boxes after a transfer and use the recipient total for the final draw
svg.desc: Initially box A contains three red and two blue counters, total five, while box B contains two red and four blue counters, total six. One uniformly selected counter is transferred from A to B. Then one counter is selected uniformly from B. T means the transferred counter is red and D means the final counter selected from B is red. With probability three fifths, a red transfer leaves A with two red and two blue and B with three red and four blue. With probability two fifths, a blue transfer leaves A with three red and one blue and B with two red and five blue. In both cases B now contains seven counters. The four joint routes are T and D nine thirty-fifths, T and D prime twelve thirty-fifths, T prime and D four thirty-fifths, and T prime and D prime ten thirty-fifths. The final red probability is thirteen thirty-fifths. Given the final counter is red, the probability that the transferred counter was red is nine thirteenths. No second draw is made from the donor box; its updated count is shown to distinguish it from the receiving box.
